This document lists the testing procedure P1, which must be performed on an 
annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above title block

The type 
 IFC53A Relays are extended range, single phase very inverse time over 
 current relays. This type is likely to provide faster over all protection.

The 
 variation in the magnitude of fault current thru the relay is dependent upon 
 the location of the fault with respect to the relay. The applications of 
 these relays requires three relays for multiphase fault protection one per 
 phase, and a separate relay connected for single phase to ground faults.

The first draft initiated by 
 eng. Fayza El-Sharkawy, tested by eng. Shirin 
 Hamdy & eng. Azza Salama, revised by EDEP Co. Quality Control 
 eng. Adel El-Nagar, accepted by General Director eng. Mahmoud Saker and approved 
 by eng. Moustfa Alam Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should 
 carry the suitable safety category

Safety 
 fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area is 
 required.

 for test

Look at field maintenance file and 
 compare the position of the setting switches on relay with those shown on 
 the setting sheet.

Connect the test leads between the relay 
 current terminals ( 3-4 ).

Connect the test leads between the relay 
 contacts ( 1-2 ) .

Increase the current slowly until the 
 relay picks up.

Record the pick up value in the test 
 sheet.

Increase the current to the values ( 2 In, 
 5 In & 10 In) where In is the rating current, until the relay trips at 
 every current value.

Record the trip time value at each current 
 value in the test sheet

Technical Procedure
Procedure:
 Testing Procedure(s) 
 (P1-Y1)
Introduction
This document lists the testing procedure P1, which must be performed on an 
annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above title block
The type 
 IFC53A Relays are extended range, single phase very inverse time over 
 current relays. This type is likely to provide faster over all protection.
The 
 variation in the magnitude of fault current thru the relay is dependent upon 
 the location of the fault with respect to the relay. The applications of 
 these relays requires three relays for multiphase fault protection one per 
 phase, and a separate relay connected for single phase to ground faults.
The first draft initiated by 
 eng. Fayza El-Sharkawy, tested by eng. Shirin 
 Hamdy & eng. Azza Salama, revised by EDEP Co. Quality Control 
 eng. Adel El-Nagar, accepted by General Director eng. Mahmoud Saker and approved 
 by eng. Moustfa Alam Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should 
 carry the suitable safety category
Safety 
 fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area is 
 required.

 carry the suitable safety category
Safety 
 fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area is 
 required.
The generator must be out of service.
Tools and Equipment
Test Plugs.
Test Leads.
Secondary Injection test set.
Work to be Carried Out
Preparation
Make sure PT secondary circuit are opened 
 at the incoming terminal blocks before isolating the relay voltage circuit 
 for test
Look at field maintenance file and 
 compare the position of the setting switches on relay with those shown on 
 the setting sheet.
Testing the Relay
Connect the test leads between the relay 
 current terminals ( 3-4 ).
Connect the test leads between the relay 
 contacts ( 1-2 ) .
Increase the current slowly until the 
 relay picks up.
Record the pick up value in the test 
 sheet.
Increase the current to the values ( 2 In, 
 5 In & 10 In) where In is the rating current, until the relay trips at 
 every current value.
Record the trip time value at each current 
 value in the test sheet
